p.x:
My best friend is Ploy. We met on our first day at secondary school. I was nervous and a little afraid because I didn't know anyone, and I felt very lonely at lunchtime. Then Ploy came and sat next to me. She smiled and said, "Do you want to share my snacks?" We have been friends ever since.
Ploy is very kind and very funny. When I'm sad, she always makes me laugh. She is also good at listening. Last year, when my grandmother was ill, Ploy came to my house every day after school. I will never forget that.
Next month, Ploy is moving to Chiang Mai with her family. I'm happy for her, but I'm also worried that we won't see each other often. She has invited me to visit her in the holidays, and I'm already excited about the trip. My mother says real friends stay friends, even when they live far away.

p.t: The Surprise Party That Went Wrong
p.x:
Last month, Ben decided to organise a surprise party for his girlfriend Mia's 25th birthday. He invited thirty friends, booked a restaurant and asked everyone to keep it a secret. Unfortunately, Mia saw a message on Ben's phone the day before and thought he was planning a date with another woman. She was so jealous and annoyed that she didn't speak to him all evening.
The next day, Ben had to explain everything. At first, Mia felt embarrassed, then relieved, and finally very grateful. "I'm sorry I didn't trust you," she said. She apologised to Ben, and they laughed about it. The party went ahead, but Mia had to pretend to be surprised.
Ben was a little disappointed that the surprise was ruined, but he says it taught him something. "Mia's friends gave her a lot of support that night. Even though she knew about the party, she was in a great mood and felt really confident about our relationship."

Empathy, the ability to imagine how another person feels, is often described as the foundation of friendship. Psychologists distinguish it from sympathy: a sympathetic friend feels sorry for you, while an empathetic one tries to understand your situation from the inside. Both are valuable, but research suggests that empathy builds deeper trust.
Showing empathy requires us to be a little vulnerable ourselves. When a friend is overwhelmed or insecure, sharing our own struggles can make them feel less alone. Compassion, the desire to help, often follows naturally.
Of course, no friendship is perfect. Most of us have felt betrayed at some point, perhaps when a secret was shared or a promise broken. In such moments, resentment can grow quickly, and many friendships end. Yet researchers have found that friends who manage to reconcile after a serious argument often become closer than before. The key, it seems, is honest conversation rather than silence.
Interestingly, studies show that even a casual acquaintance can provide surprising emotional support. People who were devastated by a loss often say that a kind word from a neighbour or colleague meant a great deal. Empathy, in other words, is not only for our closest friends.

q.s: She is very ___. She always helps other people.
q.en: People who help others are kind. After 'is' we need an adjective.
q.th: คนที่ช่วยเหลือผู้อื่นคือคนใจดี (kind) หลัง is ใช้คุณศัพท์

การช่วยเหลือไม่ได้แสดงความโกรธ
การช่วยเหลือไม่ได้แสดงความเศร้า

q.s: Why are you ___? – Because my cat is ill.
q.en: A sick cat makes you sad.
q.th: แมวป่วยทำให้เศร้า
x: A sick cat doesn't make you happy.
แมวป่วยไม่ทำให้มีความสุข
A sick cat isn't a reason to be funny.
แมวป่วยไม่ใช่เหตุผลที่จะตลก
Kind is not a feeling caused by a sick cat.
kind ไม่ใช่ความรู้สึกที่เกิดจากแมวป่วย

q.s: My little brother is very ___. He makes everyone laugh.
q.en: A funny person makes people laugh.
q.th: คนตลก (funny) ทำให้คนอื่นหัวเราะ
x: Angry people don't make others laugh.
คนโกรธไม่ทำให้คนหัวเราะ

ความเหนื่อยไม่ทำให้คนหัวเราะ

q.s: Don't be ___ with me! It wasn't my fault.

q.th: It wasn't my fault แสดงว่าอีกฝ่ายกำลังโกรธ
x: ไม่พูดว่า อย่ามีความสุข
ไม่พูดว่า อย่าใจดี
ไม่เข้ากับ not my fault

q.s: I'm so ___ about the trip to Japan! I can't wait!
q.en: 'I can't wait' shows a happy feeling about the future: excited. People feel '-ed'.
q.th: I can't wait แสดงความรู้สึกตื่นเต้น คนรู้สึกใช้ -ed: excited
x: '-ing' describes the thing: an exciting trip.
-ing ใช้บรรยายสิ่งของ: an exciting trip
Bored people don't say 'I can't wait!'
คนเบื่อไม่พูดว่า I can't wait
ความกังวลไม่เข้ากับ I can't wait

q.s: He was ___ before his first job interview, so his hands were shaking.
q.en: Shaking hands show he was nervous.
q.th: มือสั่นแสดงว่าประหม่า (nervous)
x: Pride doesn't make hands shake before an interview.
ความภูมิใจไม่ทำให้มือสั่น
คนเบื่อมือไม่สั่น
Loneliness isn't connected with an interview.
ความเหงาไม่เกี่ยวกับการสัมภาษณ์

q.s: Let's ___ Mai to our party. She's new in our class.
q.en: 'Let's' + base verb: Let's invite.
q.th: Let's + กริยาช่อง 1: Let's invite
x: invitation เป็นคำนาม
หลัง let's ไม่ใช้ -ing
หลัง let's ไม่มี to

q.s: My parents were very ___ of me when I passed the exam.
q.en: 'Be proud of someone' is the phrase.
q.th: วลีคือ be proud of someone = ภูมิใจในตัว...
x: pride เป็นคำนาม
proudly เป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์
We say 'happy for someone', not 'happy of'.
ต้องพูดว่า happy for ไม่ใช่ happy of

q.s: I felt really ___ when I forgot my teacher's name.
q.en: People feel '-ed': I felt embarrassed.
q.th: คนรู้สึกใช้ -ed: I felt embarrassed
x: '-ing' describes the situation: an embarrassing moment.
-ing ใช้บรรยายสถานการณ์
embarrass เป็นกริยา
embarrassment เป็นคำนาม

q.s: He's ___ of his brother because their parents give his brother more attention.
q.en: Jealous = unhappy because someone has something you want.
q.th: jealous = อิจฉา
x: 'nervous of' isn't the right feeling here.
nervous ไม่ใช่ความรู้สึกที่ถูกต้องในที่นี้

q.en: 'I apologise for…' is a formal way to say sorry.
q.th: I apologise for... = ขอโทษสำหรับ... (ทางการ)
x: apology เป็นคำนาม
I excuse for ไม่ถูกต้อง
The other person forgives; you apologise.
อีกฝ่ายเป็นคนให้อภัย (forgive)

q.s: I was so ___ when the doctor said it was nothing serious.
q.en: Relieved = happy because a worry has gone.
q.th: relieved = โล่งใจ
x: relief เป็นคำนาม
'relaxing' describes a thing, not your feeling.
relaxing ใช้บรรยายสิ่งของ
released = ถูกปล่อย

q.s: A good nurse needs ___: the ability to understand how patients feel.
q.en: Empathy = understanding other people's feelings.
q.th: empathy = ความเข้าใจความรู้สึกผู้อื่น
x: apathy = ความเฉยเมย ไม่สนใจ
envy = ความอิจฉา

q.en: Reconcile = become friends again after an argument.
q.th: reconcile = คืนดีกัน
x: 'reminded' needs an object and means help someone remember.
reminded = เตือนความจำ

q.s: [Him] is my best [friend] [and] [he] is very kind.
q.fix: He is my best friend and he is very kind.
q.en: The subject must be 'He', not 'Him'.
q.th: ประธานต้องใช้ He ไม่ใช่ Him

q.s: My friends [is] [very] [funny] [and] kind.
q.fix: My friends are very funny and kind.
q.en: 'My friends' is plural, so 'are'.
q.th: My friends เป็นพหูพจน์ ใช้ are

q.s: I [feel] [lonely] [because] all my friends [are going] abroad last month.
q.fix: I feel lonely because all my friends went abroad last month.
q.en: 'Last month' is finished past: Past Simple 'went'.
q.th: last month เป็นอดีต ใช้ Past Simple: went

q.s: She was [so] [surprising] [when] she [saw] the cake.
q.fix: She was so surprised when she saw the cake.
q.en: People feel '-ed': surprised. 'Surprising' describes the thing.
q.th: คนรู้สึกใช้ -ed: surprised ส่วน surprising ใช้กับสิ่งของ

q.s: Everything [will] be [fine], so [don't] [worried].
q.fix: Everything will be fine, so don't worry.
q.en: After 'don't' (imperative) we use the base verb: don't worry.
q.th: หลัง don't (ประโยคคำสั่ง) ใช้กริยาช่อง 1: don't worry

q.s: She [apologised] [for] [to be] rude [to] me.
q.fix: She apologised for being rude to me.
q.en: After a preposition (for) we use verb-ing: for being.
q.th: หลังบุพบท (for) ใช้ V-ing: for being
x: apologise for ถูกต้อง
rude to ถูกต้อง

q.s: I'm [grateful] [to] my friends [for] [help] me.
q.fix: I'm grateful to my friends for helping me.
q.en: After 'for' we use verb-ing: for helping.
q.th: หลัง for ใช้ V-ing: for helping
x: grateful to ถูกต้อง
grateful for ถูกต้อง

q.s: [Annoying] by the noise, he closed the window [and] [put on] [his] headphones.
q.fix: Annoyed by the noise, he closed the window and put on his headphones.
q.en: He felt annoyed (passive meaning: the noise annoyed him), so we use the '-ed' form.
q.th: เขารู้สึกรำคาญ (เสียงทำให้รำคาญ) จึงใช้รูป -ed: Annoyed
x: put on ถูกต้อง

q.s: If she [hadn't] [betrayed] my trust, we [would be still] friends [now].
q.fix: If she hadn't betrayed my trust, we would still be friends now.
q.en: Adverbs like 'still' go between 'would' and 'be': would still be.
q.th: กริยาวิเศษณ์อย่าง still วางระหว่าง would กับ be: would still be
x: 'hadn't' is correct in a mixed conditional.
'now' is correct for a present result.

q.s: It's [no use] [to apologise] now; the damage [has] [already] been done.
q.fix: It's no use apologising now; the damage has already been done.
q.en: 'It's no use' is followed by verb-ing.
q.th: It's no use ตามด้วย V-ing
x: no use ถูกต้อง

เป็นการปฏิเสธ

q.th: ข่าวดี B จึงแสดงความยินดี
x: ใช้กับการสอบตก

q.s:

q.en: B understands and accepts the apology.
q.th: B เข้าใจและรับคำขอโทษ
x: It's angry, which contradicts 'You've been so busy'.
แสดงความโกรธ ขัดกับ You've been so busy
ขัดกับน้ำเสียงที่เข้าใจ
A ลืม ไม่ได้จำ

q.s:
A: Can I tell you a secret?
B: ___
o: Of course. You can trust me.

q.th: B ตกลงและสัญญาว่าจะเก็บความลับ
x: ไม่สมเหตุผล

q.s:
A: I feel so overwhelmed with everything at the moment.
B: ___
o: Do you want to talk about it? Maybe I can help.

q.th: B แสดงความเห็นใจและเสนอช่วย
x: การรับมือไม่ไหวไม่ใช่เรื่องสนุก

q.s:

o: We never speak to anyone again.
q.en: 'In such moments, resentment can grow quickly.'
q.th: ในช่วงนั้น ความขุ่นเคืองอาจเพิ่มขึ้นอย่างรวดเร็ว
x: Only if they reconcile, and not always.
เฉพาะเมื่อคืนดีกัน และไม่เสมอไป
เกินจริง ไม่ได้บอก

q.s: What have researchers found about friends who reconcile after a serious argument?
o: They often become closer than before.
q.en: 'Friends who manage to reconcile… often become closer than before.'
q.th: เพื่อนที่คืนดีกันได้มักสนิทกันมากกว่าเดิม
x: 'The key is honest conversation rather than silence.'
กุญแจคือการพูดคุยอย่างจริงใจ ไม่ใช่ความเงียบ

q.s: What is the main point of the last paragraph?
o: Even people we don't know well can comfort us.
Only close friends can help us.
q.en: 'Even a casual acquaintance can provide surprising emotional support.'
q.th: แม้แต่คนรู้จักห่างๆ ก็ให้กำลังใจได้อย่างน่าประหลาดใจ
x: A neighbour's kind word 'meant a great deal'.
คำพูดดีๆ จากเพื่อนบ้านมีความหมายมาก
